hook: Chile's Atacama Desert just transformed into a massive floral display covering 7,000 square miles.

sections.voiceover: Chile's Atacama Desert just transformed into a massive floral display covering 7,000 square miles.
sections.visual_cue: Wide drone shot of the Atacama Desert landscape transitioning from sand to a carpet of flowers.
sections.sfx_cue: Wind transition into soft, ambient desert sounds.
b_roll: Drone footage of Atacama Desert landscape

sections.voiceover: Record-breaking El Niño rains flooded the parched Atacama Desert, creating an unexpected botanical explosion. How did millions of dormant seeds and bulbs in the Atacama Desert suddenly wake up?
sections.visual_cue: Map of Chile highlighting the Atacama region with rain animation overlay.

sections.voiceover: But these dormant Atacama Desert seeds waited decades for the heaviest rainfall since 1950.
sections.visual_cue: Close-up macro shot of tiny seeds buried in dry, cracked desert earth.

sections.voiceover: The El Niño super cycle finally triggered this massive floral bloom across the Atacama Desert. Millions of bulbs sprouted simultaneously, covering 7,000 square miles of the parched Atacama Desert landscape.
sections.visual_cue: Sweeping cinematic pans showing fields of purple and yellow flowers stretching to the horizon.
b_roll: Cinematic pans of blooming Atacama desert

sections.voiceover: This is the biggest floral display in the Atacama Desert since records began in 1950.
sections.visual_cue: Slow zoom out to reveal the scale of the floral display against the mountain backdrop.
